item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Antiplatelet

lookback_source.quote: N0415I1. Antiplatelet: Check if an antiplatelet medication (e.g., aspirin/extended release, dipyridamole, clopidogrel) was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back/observation period, or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days. The manual uses the phrases "7-day observation period" (N0415I1/I2, p. N-8) and "7-day look-back period" (item set instruction, p. N-4) interchangeably for this item set. The document does not state how the window is counted relative to the ARD on these pages.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code antiplatelet medications such as aspirin/extended release, dipyridamole, or clopidogrel as N0415E, Anticoagulant.

source.quote: Do not code antiplatelet medications such as aspirin/extended release, dipyridamole, or clopidogrel as N0415E, Anticoagulant.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how the medication is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415Z1, None of the above, if none of the listed medications (including antiplatelet) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Medical record documentation that the medication was received by the resident and documentation of the indication for its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Step 1 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: Documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room) must be reviewed.

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Step 2 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: An "indication" must be the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but with an expectation that the source is identifiable.

federal.criterion: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed reference resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

conflicts.topic: Terminology of the observation window for N0415I ("7-day observation period" vs. "7-day look-back period")

positions.claim: N0415I1 states the window as the "7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)."

source.quote: was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: The N0415 item form states the window as "during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days," and other rows in the same list (e.g., N0415H1) use "7-day look-back period."

source.quote: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification, not how it is used, during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days

conflicts.resolution: Not a substantive difference in length: both describe a 7-day window (or since admission/entry or reentry if shorter). Terminology difference recorded; treated as the same 7-day window.
